changes.before: In §57 of the 1797 Doctrine of Right he pushes this into the position of a criterion, and the anchor turns inward: a state under attack may use any means of defence except those that would make its subjects unfit to be citizens — because then it would itself no longer qualify to exist as a person in the relations of states. The list of prohibitions that follows opens with using one's own subjects as spies, then assassins, poisoners, and those employed merely to spread false reports.
changes.after: In §57 of the 1797 Doctrine of Right he pushes this into the position of a criterion, and the anchor turns inward: a state under attack may use any means of defence except those that would make its subjects unfit to be citizens — because then it would itself no longer qualify to exist as a person under international law in the relations of states. The list of prohibitions that follows opens with using one's own subjects as spies, then assassins, poisoners, and those employed merely to spread false reports.

changes.before: One note, because it affects how the rest of this essay reads: §57 and the 1795 article are substantially continuous and form no tension. The concern in both is the same — no means that would destroy post-war trust — and §57 says more precisely what gets destroyed first: your own people. Fighting with spies, assassins, poison and false reports corrupts, morally and civically, the very men who carry out the orders; and a state made of corrupted men can no longer stand as a person alongside other states. SAE's §12 says the crux of gui — the fourth grade, deceit — is the suppression of one's own side's subjecthood. The two are not the same technical proposition, and they point the same way: whether a means is disqualifying is read off what it does to the party using it.

changes.before: And there is no right and wrong here. Kant did not touch the ground. No colonizing, no enslaving, no annihilation of the state, no partition, the people keeping its original right to constitute a commonwealth — he held the anti-colonial line, and held it further forward than almost anyone of his time. So this is not he did not go far enough. It is two paths on one ground parting at this point.
changes.after: And there is no right and wrong here. Kant did not touch the ground. changes.reason: Restore 绝大多数 instead of the stronger near-universal comparison.

changes.before: The reason they part can be named. Kant's path is right. Right handles the conditions under which external coercion is possible — which coercion is legitimate and which is not. In the language of right, a constitution whose nature is unfavourable to the inclination to war is a formal property that can be identified from outside: has it put the power to declare war in the hands of those who bear the cost of war. Since the property is externally identifiable, promoting it by coercion does not exceed what right can handle. And pushed to its end, that path really does ask little of procedure: if the constraint falls on the constitution's nature, then who drafts it, whether it goes to a vote, how long it is supervised, are none of them questions the path must answer — the property obtains, the requirement is met.
changes.after: The reason they part can be named. Kant's path is juridical right. Right handles the conditions under which external coercion is possible — which coercion is legitimate and which is not. In the language of right, a constitution whose nature is unfavourable to the inclination to war is a formal property that can be identified from outside: has it put the power to declare war in the hands of those who bear the cost of war. Since the property is externally identifiable, promoting it by coercion does not exceed what right can handle. And pushed to its end, that path really does ask little of procedure: if the constraint falls on the constitution's nature, then who drafts it, whether it goes to a vote, how long it is supervised, are none of them questions the path must answer — the property obtains, the requirement is met.
changes.reason: Disambiguate 法权 from an assertion that Kant's path is correct, which would contradict the stated no-right-or-wrong distinction.

changes.before: He then explains the arrangement inside it. The state will silently invite such counsel while keeping the fact of it secret — because to ask its subjects for rules of external conduct would seem to detract from the dignity of its legislative authority. On the philosophers' side, they must be free to discuss the general maxims of war and peace publicly; the sovereign should not let that class disappear or be silenced. Eight words: speak in public, be taught in secret. changes.before: Read Kant's article against those four. Questioning: yes. Reaching the core of decision: only adjacent — taken into consideration gives a duty to consider, not a position inside the procedure of decision. The questioner is locally protected: public speech may not be forbidden and the class may not be silenced, but there is no protection from reprisal and no procedural guarantee. Actual effect on the decision is not secured: no precedence does not mean no effect, and being heard does not mean being heeded. So it is a local mechanism, and it is not closed.
changes.after: Read Kant's article against those four. Questioning: yes. changes.reason: Restore 不等于必然改变, preserving the distinction between a hearing and guaranteed change.

changes.before: Two things are downgraded here rather than claimed. That §60 prescribes no procedure is registered as a textual fact only, with nothing inferred from it. And the step any external property condition displaces the subject of cultivation is not argued in this volume, so it is booked as outstanding: SAE may draw its line earlier than Kant, and it needs an independent argument to do so, and that argument does not yet exist. Until it is finished, the claim here is only that each line needs a further stretch of road — not that SAE's stretch has been walked.

changes.before: One interpretive dispute is left unchosen — whether §60 is an independent exception in ius ad bellum or belongs mainly to ius in bello and ius post bellum — since neither reading affects the argument. And one debt is booked without an answer. Kant's exception for a divided state covers the case where a country splits in two, each part claiming to be an independent state representing the whole. When both parts claim in the first person to represent the whole, which bearing-position does do not perform the reconstitution protect? How is an outside actor to tell, without the telling itself completing the legislation for the whole? Kant gives when assistance stops counting as interference. What he does not give, and SAE has not given either, is how to identify the legitimate bearer among competing claims of representation.
